Undoing a derivative

Placeholder paragraph for the test fixture. A derivative tells how fast a function changes; an antiderivative goes the other way and recovers a function from its rate of change. If $F'(x) = f(x)$ then $F$ is an antiderivative of $f$, and so is $F(x) + C$ for every constant $C$, because a constant has derivative zero. The power rule read backward gives $\int x^n\,dx = \frac{x^{n+1}}{n+1} + C$ for $n \ne -1$, and the derivatives of sine, cosine, $e^x$ and $\ln x$ read backward give their antiderivatives. Always check an answer by differentiating it: the derivative of the answer must be the integrand.
